reviews.author: Cheri P.
reviews.text: Beautiful Park with some amazing old growth trees. Lots of trails through the wooded area for bike or walking there is a steep incline. Most views are from the cliffs. The beach access and campground were closed at the beginning of April. Saw lots of birds and sea lions from a far on the cliffs. Bring your binoculars. Coast Guard area is not open to visitors.

reviews.author: Julia F.
reviews.text:
Lovely views all around! Roads were reasonably well-kept and easy to navigate for most vehicles. Some pretty patchy areas that may not be fun on a motorcycle, so if you're a rider keep your eyes out.

The North Head Lighthouse (pictured) was a very easy walk to get to, fully pathed and only gentle slopes. All the parking areas had easy turnarounds, well kept notice boards, and plenty of bathrooms around.

A very nice place to check out while you're in the area!

reviews.author: Nati's T.
reviews.text:
As you have likely heard, you won't be disappointed... unless it is a cold wet rainy PNW day and you dressed wrong.

So, dress right and have fun - whatever for the weather (good luck, its always changing. Personally, rain jacket and pants stay in the car.)

Of course, I was lucky to be there on a lovely sunny day 😛

reviews.author: Jessica E.
reviews.text: What a beautiful place to sight see, hiking trails to explore, 10$ to park I think, I visited this to go to bells viewpoint for the first time and it did not disappoint, first time at a light house too

reviews.author: Shubhro B.
reviews.text:
This state park is a hidden gem in Washington. The beach is very beautiful, with sandy shores, stunning views, lighthouse in the backdrop, and easy access to the waterfront. Lots of jelly fish wash up to the shore - something unique. The state park has several fun hikes. The ones worth mention are the hikes to the Dead Man’s Cove and the one leading all the way up to the Lighthouse. Dead Man’s Cove offers some amazing secluded views, and the hike up to this spot is fun and moderate. The hike leading up to the Lighthouse tends to get a little steep towards the end, but is worth it. The views from the base of the Lighthouse are breathtaking. Lots of natural beauty, variety of birds, and sounds of nature to sit back and enjoy from your campsite.

We stayed in one of the log cabins and had a great experience. Our cabin was very well maintained, had fully functional heaters, electrical points, and some additional furniture. Just like any other log cabin, you’d need to bring along your bed supplies to make it comfortably to the bunk beds. The only thing we didnt like was the close proximity of the other camp sites. It offered very little privacy. There are several dining options in the area. We went to the Salt Pub and had a very good experience. The food and drinks were great, hosts very welcoming.

Overall, I’d highly recommend this state park, and the camp sites - its a nature lover’s delight.

reviews.author: Larissa T
reviews.text: Went here and was not disappointed everything was beautiful, everyone was very nice, lighthouses were awesome and so was fort Canby, it’s common sense not to leave food out in the woods, the raccoons ate our cookies but we weren’t mad, the lady working at cape d’ store remembered our coffee order after one day beautiful lush forests all around with the sound of the ocean in the background, saw seals over at the boat launch
reviews.title: It's NOT disappointing!

reviews.author: tgrdvrmd
reviews.text: Our tour group visited here and the views are awesome. The fog cleared and we could see the Columbia bar area and the surrounding waterways. The lighthouse is really interesting as is the visitor center. We were here 3 years ago and is certainly worth the effort to go.

reviews.author: LynnS290
reviews.text:
Beautiful area. Lots of walking paths. The path to the old lighthouse is a climb through the forest path lined with gnarled tree roots - not a walk for folks who are physically challenged. The path to the north lighthouse is paved so much easier to walk, plus they have a few benches along the way. Fun gift shops.

The photo opps are many and oh so gorgeous

You need a Discovery Pass for the park. Can buy on premises for $10 a day or online for $11.50. Be sure to put your car's plate number on your tag or you may get a ticket on your car

reviews.author: Meeta P
reviews.text: I booked 2 campsites in loop D near Lake O ‘ Neil in Cape Disappointment state park in January. My camping experience was ruined because of the mess created by raccoons. We reached our campsite after sunset and kept a bag of unopened chips on the picnic table before we started setting up the tents. In less than 5 min of our arrival the raccoon stole the bag of chips and tried to escape. So it was clear that we couldn’t have any food outside. That was a bummer. I had called the park to check if Loop D sites were operating and had no issues. It would have been helpful if the park office warned us of raccoons attacking campsites. We would have better prepared ourselves. Even after no food was kept outside while we were sitting by the campfire the raccoons were roaming the campsite multiple times. So we couldn’t be relaxed and always had to be vigilant of their presence. My request to the park is please put up signs to be aware of raccoons to not take out food even when you are present at your campsite. All campsites in loop D are not well maintained. The one good part was washrooms were clean with hot water and hot showers. Overall the loop D campsites need a lot of maintenance for safety of campers.

reviews.author: Diana Richards G
reviews.text: We went on a rainy day, which just immersed us in the Lewis & Clark experience at the interpretive center. We couldn’t see long distances because it was overcast and rainy, but it was fun to drive out on the jetty and spend some time learning about the Lewis & Clark adventure. If you like history and learning about the early explorers this is an excellent place to visit.
reviews.title: Does. Not. Disappoint.

reviews.author: Vangen007
reviews.text: Fantastic Sate Park with tons to do. Camping has been great. They also have yurts and clean restrooms. We took the dogs down the light house trail today. Great place to come rain or shine.

reviews.author: hollyrk9
reviews.text: It was disappointing that the light house trail was closed, but otherwise it was a nice walk and views where we could go. The parking ticket thing didn't work, not sure if it was our banks blocking the transaction because we were out of state or just the machine not working (yes we had plenty of funds and tried multiple cards), so we didn't want to stay too long to avoid getting a ticket.

reviews.author: Wildwoodatheart
reviews.text: I was here over Labor Day weekend. It was a bit crowded, but still worth the visit! The best way to see the Washington State Parks is to buy a yearly Discover Pass. It's only $30, which is good for a year. If you only buy a day pass, it is $10. Do the math. Plus you are helping to fund the parks and keep them safe and clean. I was there early enough in the day that I found parking easily in the places I visited. People were really good about wearing masks and social distancing. I was with my dog, and she really enjoyed our visit too. We found our way to Waikiki Beach with great views of Cape Disappointment Lighthouse. We also visited the North lighthouse as well. That trail was a bit crowded, but we were able to keep away from other people. The views all around were good, even though there was smoke in the air from the Northwest fires. In driving past the campgrounds, they looked nice. This park is well worth a day trip, and it seems like a great place to camp!

reviews.author: Xterra r
reviews.text: We spent two separate days in the park. The first was very foggy and we weren't able to see anything from the view points. We did walk the north jetty and the waves were fantastic! Lots of people fishing and it was fascinating to see the huge fish they were catching. The second day was on a high wind day and it was fun to try to stand upright in the wind at the North Lighthouse. We were glad that we went back up to the visitor center for the views across the river and out to the ocean when a storm was approaching. The weather viewpoint is dramatic. We did try to go to Waikiki beach but the blowing sand made it hard to stare out into the ocean. It was fun to watch the drift wood pile up on the shore with the force of the wind.

Just returned from Cape Disappointment State Park and for the most part enjoyed our trip. We stated at the campground in the non-serviced part(site 211), closest to the entrance. The spot was just fine and I actually preferred this area over the serviced sites at the beach. Our spot was grassy and butted up to the lake. It also was a close walk to Waikiki beach which is a great beach. I much preferred it to Benson Beach because it was more protected and I actually felt ok with my 2 1/2 year old playing in the gentle waves. It was also less windy.

So much to do in the area. Lots of fun hikes and the Lewis and Clark museum was wonderful. I was a little disappointed that you cannot take children under 7 up in the light houses though. Close to Long Beach and Astoria. Seriously, the outdoor and fun activities make this place worth going....

However, two things that I didn't like - the ranger volunteer lady trying to upsale me to a better spot which would require moving 3 times during our stay and the weather, which I am not sure what is normal for this area, but it was cold, foggy and so windy, even in July. The wind was so bad that we didn't even go outside at night because it was so cold. But that is mother nature and uncontrollable, so I can't really complain about that. So, that might distract me from going there again because you go camping to be outside and I felt like I really missed that.
reviews.title: Wonderful location and activities

reviews.text:
I had a reservation for Friday, March 21 to Sunday, March 23. I arrived after hours and just drove right in to my campsite. The campground is set up in sections A, B, C, and D. Section D is near the entrance along a lake. The other sections are down a long drive close to the beach. Section C was closed. Each section is divided into smaller circles of 10 campsites each. Although there is not much privacy between sites, the sites are still spacious and mine backed up to woods. My trailer has a large stargazer window on the back and I was able to leave my shades open most of the time. Section A also has full hook-ups. While my loop was farthest from the beach, you could still hear the ocean which is lovely and relaxing. It's not a far walk to the beach and my toddler did it easily. Once on the beach, there is a big sign with a giant A so you can find your way back should you go for a walk. There are two lighthouses in the park, trails, jetty, and an interperative center. Once out of the park, Long Beach is a short drive. I enjoyed our time and would love to go back for a longer trip.

I got zero reception in the campground. I use Verizon.

Pros: clean, well-maintained sites. Visible park rangers who were friendly and helpful. Close to the beach. Lots of amenities and trails.

Cons: (1) the electricity is not consistent and it is weak. Like you can’t run your microwave and your electric water heater at the same time weak. Make sure you have a surge protector/line conditioner on your electrical hookup because you could seriously damage your rig plugging into this park’s electrical. (2) no cell service. Not a single bar of Verizon LTE anywhere in this campground. This wouldn’t be a big deal if we were expecting that kind of experience but, to the contrary, the Dyrt’s listing for this campground says Verizon service is good. It is not only not good, it is nonexistent. (3) once you enter the park, there are no signs directing you to the campground. The address in the confirmation email sent after we reserved our spot was not anywhere near correct. Luckily there were 2 park rangers there when we pulled in who helped us get un-lost. This is a huge state park so it is unacceptable not to have any signs that even say “campground” with an arrow. There are signs for everything else, just not the campground.

Spent a night and two days here. Don’t remember the exact spot I camped at, but it was quite close to the beach in November 2024. Really loved access to the free showers, not the hottest, but was nice for being free! Some spots are a little close to other campers, but not obnoxious. Was very quiet at the time I visited. Would certainly visit again.

reviews.author: David D.
reviews.text:
We reserved our space online with the Washington State Parks website. Very easy to use and complete our reservation. https://washington.goingtocamp.com/

We have camped at some nice spots on the Coast of Washington but Cape Disappointment was a real treat! The campsites are spacious and clean, our Camp Host Lynn was really sweet, such a lovely lady and fun to talk with. Rebecca at the gate was very pleasant as well, helpful and even gave us pointers on which area would be best for us.

The local towns were full of things to go and see, lots of activities for young folks as well as us not so young folks too. Be sure to visit the Lewis and Clark lookout and interpretive center, tons of information. Cost is $5 per person, but worth it.

Visit the North Light House as well, this is an easy walk-in sight and it has outstanding views. Sunsets were simply amazing. Just beautiful. I didn't get a chance to photo from up there but will next time we go.

Word of warning, ZERO cell service at the camp sights, don't count on it for streaming or hotspot for work. I was able to make calls from at the entrance and boat ramp.

Fishing out of Ilwaco is a fantastic way to stock your freezer, I have caught over a 100 Albacore tuna, countless rock fish, and a couple ling cod. If you enjoy crab, you can try your luck at the North Jetty.

All in all, this is a very beautiful park, we will be back at least another 4-5 times this year. (maybe more)
